57_1_1: Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus, and Timothy our brother, to Philemon — our beloved friend and fellow worker —
57_1_2: and to Apphia our sister, and to Archippus our fellow soldier, and to the church that meets in your house:
57_1_3: Grace to you, and peace, from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
57_1_4: I thank my God always when I remember you in my prayers,
57_1_5: because I keep hearing of your love and of the faith you have toward the Lord Jesus and toward all the saints.
57_1_6: And I pray that the fellowship of your faith may become effective — through the full knowledge of every good thing that is in us for Christ's sake.
57_1_7: For I have had much joy and encouragement from your love, brother — because the hearts of the saints have been refreshed through you.
57_1_8: Therefore, although I have plenty of boldness in Christ to order you to do what is fitting,
57_1_9: yet for love's sake I prefer to appeal to you. I — Paul, an old man, and now also a prisoner of Christ Jesus —
57_1_10: I appeal to you for my child, whom I have begotten in my chains: Onesimus.
57_1_11: Once he was useless to you — but now he has become truly useful, both to you and to me.
57_1_12: I am sending him back to you — that is, my own heart.
57_1_13: I would have liked to keep him with me, so that on your behalf he might serve me in my chains for the gospel.
57_1_14: But without your consent I did not want to do anything, so that your good deed would not be by compulsion, but of your own free will.
57_1_15: For perhaps this is why he was separated from you for a little while — so that you might have him back forever:
57_1_16: no longer as a slave, but more than a slave — a beloved brother, especially to me, but how much more to you, both in the flesh and in the Lord.
57_1_17: So if you consider me a partner, welcome him as you would welcome me.
57_1_18: And if he has wronged you in any way, or owes you anything, charge that to my account.
57_1_19: I, Paul, am writing this with my own hand: I will repay it — without mentioning that you owe me even your own self.
57_1_20: Yes, brother — let me have some benefit from you in the Lord. Refresh my heart in Christ.
57_1_21: Confident of your obedience, I write to you — knowing that you will do even more than I say.
57_1_22: And one thing more — prepare a guest room for me, for I am hoping that through your prayers I will be given back to you.
57_1_23: Epaphras — my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus — sends you greetings,
57_1_24: as do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke — my fellow workers.
57_1_25: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.
65_1_1: Jude, a servant of Jesus Christ and brother of James — to those who are called, beloved in God the Father, and kept for Jesus Christ:
65_1_2: May mercy, peace, and love be multiplied to you.
65_1_3: Beloved, while I was making every effort to write to you about our common salvation, I found it necessary to write urging you to contend earnestly for the faith — once for all delivered to the saints.
65_1_4: For certain men have crept in unnoticed — those who long ago were marked out for this condemnation. They are ungodly, perverting the grace of our God into licentiousness, and denying the only Master and our Lord, Jesus Christ.
65_1_5: Now I want to remind you — though you already know all this — that the Lord, having once saved a people out of the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed those who did not believe.
65_1_6: And the angels who did not keep their proper position, but abandoned their own dwelling — He has kept in eternal chains under darkness for the judgment of the great Day.
65_1_7: Just so, Sodom and Gomorrah and the surrounding cities — which in like manner gave themselves over to sexual immorality and went after strange flesh — are set forth as an example, undergoing the punishment of eternal fire.
65_1_8: Yet in the same way these dreamers also defile the flesh, reject authority, and revile glorious beings.
65_1_9: But Michael the archangel, when contending with the devil and disputing about the body of Moses, did not dare bring against him a railing accusation — but said, "The Lord rebuke you!"
65_1_10: But these revile whatever they do not understand, and what they do understand by instinct — like irrational animals — these are the things by which they are destroyed.
65_1_11: Woe to them! For they have gone the way of Cain. They have rushed for profit into Balaam's error. They have perished in Korah's rebellion.
65_1_12: These are the hidden reefs at your love feasts — feasting with you fearlessly, shepherding only themselves: clouds without water, carried along by winds; autumn trees, fruitless, twice dead, uprooted;
65_1_13: wild waves of the sea, foaming up their own shame; wandering stars, for whom the gloom of darkness has been reserved forever.
65_1_14: It was also about these men that Enoch — the seventh from Adam — prophesied, saying: "Behold, the Lord came with myriads of His holy ones,
65_1_15: to execute judgment upon all, and to convict every soul of all the ungodly works they have committed in their ungodliness, and of all the harsh things ungodly sinners have spoken against Him."
65_1_16: These are grumblers, complainers, walking according to their own lusts. Their mouths speak arrogant words, flattering people for the sake of advantage.
65_1_17: But you, beloved, remember the words spoken beforehand by the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ —
65_1_18: how they kept telling you, "In the last time there will be mockers, walking according to their own ungodly lusts."
65_1_19: These are the ones who divide, who are unspiritual, devoid of the Spirit.
65_1_20: But you, beloved, building yourselves up in your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Spirit,
65_1_21: keep yourselves in the love of God — waiting for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ that brings eternal life.
65_1_22: And on some have mercy — those who waver;
65_1_23: save others, snatching them out of the fire; and on some have mercy with fear — hating even the garment stained by the flesh.
65_1_24: Now to Him who is able to keep you from stumbling, and to present you faultless before the presence of His glory with great joy —
65_1_25: to the only God our Savior, through Jesus Christ our Lord, be glory and majesty, dominion and authority, before all time, now, and forevermore. Amen.
56_1_1: Paul, a bondservant of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ — for the faith of God's chosen ones, and for the full knowledge of the truth that leads to godliness,
56_1_2: in the hope of eternal life — which God, who cannot lie, promised before the ages of time began,
56_1_3: and at the proper time has manifested His word through the proclamation entrusted to me by the command of God our Savior:
56_1_4: to Titus, my true son in our common faith — grace and peace from God the Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ our Savior.
56_1_5: For this reason I left you in Crete: that you might set in order what was lacking, and appoint elders in every city, just as I commanded you —
56_1_6: if anyone is above reproach, the husband of one wife, having children who believe and who are not accused of dissipation or rebellion.
56_1_7: For an overseer must be above reproach as God's steward — not arrogant, not quick-tempered, not given to wine, not violent, not greedy for gain;
56_1_8: but hospitable, a lover of what is good, sober-minded, righteous, holy, and self-controlled —
56_1_9: holding fast to the faithful word as he was taught, so that he may be able both to encourage by sound doctrine and to refute those who contradict.
56_1_10: For there are many rebellious men, empty talkers and deceivers — especially those of the circumcision —
56_1_11: whose mouths must be silenced. They are upsetting whole households by teaching, for the sake of dishonest gain, things they ought not to teach.
56_1_12: One of them — a prophet of their own — said, "Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, lazy gluttons."
56_1_13: This testimony is true. For this reason, rebuke them sharply — so that they may be sound in the faith,
56_1_14: not paying attention to Jewish myths or to the commands of men who turn away from the truth.
56_1_15: To the pure, all things are pure — but to those who are defiled and unbelieving, nothing is pure. Both their mind and their conscience are defiled.
56_1_16: They claim to know God, but by their deeds they deny Him — being detestable, disobedient, and unfit for any good work.
56_2_1: But as for you, speak the things that are fitting for sound doctrine.
56_2_2: Older men are to be sober-minded, dignified, self-controlled — sound in faith, in love, and in steadfastness.
56_2_3: Older women likewise — that they be reverent in behavior, not slanderers, not enslaved to much wine, teachers of what is good —
56_2_4: so that they may train the younger women to love their husbands, to love their children,
56_2_5: to be self-controlled, pure, working at home, kind, submissive to their own husbands — so that the word of God will not be discredited.
56_2_6: Likewise, urge the younger men to be self-controlled.
56_2_7: In all things show yourself to be an example of good works — in your teaching showing integrity, dignity,
56_2_8: and sound speech that cannot be condemned — so that the opponent may be put to shame, having nothing evil to say about us.
56_2_9: Bondservants are to be subject to their own masters in everything, and to be well-pleasing — not arguing back,
56_2_10: not pilfering, but showing all good faith — so that in everything they may adorn the doctrine of God our Savior.
56_2_11: For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all people,
56_2_12: training us to renounce ungodliness and worldly desires, and to live sensibly, righteously, and godly in this present age,
56_2_13: looking for the blessed hope and glorious appearing of our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ —
56_2_14: who gave Himself for us, to redeem us from all lawlessness and to purify for Himself a people for His own possession, zealous for good works.
56_2_15: These things speak — and exhort and rebuke with all authority. Let no one disregard you.
56_3_1: Remind them to be subject to rulers and authorities, to be obedient, to be ready for every good work,
56_3_2: to malign no one, to be peaceable and gentle, showing all humility to all people.
56_3_3: For we ourselves were once foolish, disobedient, deceived — slaves to various lusts and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful, and hating one another.
56_3_4: But when the kindness and the love of God our Savior toward man appeared,
56_3_5: He saved us — not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to His mercy — through the washing of regeneration and the renewing of the Holy Spirit,
56_3_6: which He poured out on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Savior,
56_3_7: so that, having been justified by His grace, we should become heirs according to the hope of eternal life.
56_3_8: This saying is faithful — and concerning these things I want you to insist confidently, so that those who have believed in God may be careful to engage in good works. These things are good and profitable for people.
56_3_9: But avoid foolish controversies, genealogies, strife, and quarrels about the law — for they are useless and worthless.
56_3_10: Reject a divisive man after the first and second admonition,
56_3_11: knowing that such a one is warped and sinful — being self-condemned.
56_3_12: When I send Artemas to you, or Tychicus, make every effort to come to me at Nicopolis — for I have decided to spend the winter there.
56_3_13: Diligently send Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their way, so that nothing is lacking for them.
56_3_14: And let our people learn to engage in good works for cases of urgent need — so that they will not be unfruitful.
56_3_15: All who are with me greet you. Greet those who love us in the faith. Grace be with you all. Amen.
53_1_1: Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy — to the church of the Thessalonians, in God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ:
53_1_2: Grace to you, and peace, from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
53_1_3: We are bound to thank God always for you, brothers, as is fitting — because your faith is growing exceedingly, and the love of every one of you for one another is abounding.
53_1_4: Therefore we ourselves boast about you among the churches of God — for your steadfastness and faith in all your persecutions and the afflictions you are enduring.
53_1_5: This is plain evidence of God's righteous judgment — that you may be counted worthy of the kingdom of God, for which you are also suffering.
53_1_6: For after all, it is just with God to repay with affliction those who afflict you,
53_1_7: and to give relief to you who are afflicted, and to us as well — when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven with His mighty angels,
53_1_8: in flaming fire, taking vengeance on those who do not know God and who do not obey the gospel of our Lord Jesus.
53_1_9: These will pay the penalty of eternal destruction, away from the presence of the Lord and from the glory of His might —
53_1_10: when He comes on that Day to be glorified in His saints and to be marveled at by all who have believed (because our testimony among you was believed).
53_1_11: To this end we always pray for you — that our God may count you worthy of His calling, and may fulfill every good resolve and every work of faith with power,
53_1_12: so that the name of our Lord Jesus may be glorified in you, and you in Him, according to the grace of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ.
53_2_1: Now we ask you, brothers, concerning the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our being gathered together to Him —
53_2_2: that you not be quickly shaken in mind, or alarmed — either by a spirit, or by a word, or by a letter seeming to be from us — to the effect that the day of the Lord has already come.
53_2_3: Let no one deceive you in any way. For that day will not come unless the falling away comes first, and the man of lawlessness is revealed — the son of destruction —
53_2_4: the one who opposes and exalts himself against every so-called god or object of worship, so that he takes his seat in the temple of God, proclaiming himself to be God.
53_2_5: Do you not remember that, while I was still with you, I was telling you these things?
53_2_6: And now you know what is restraining him — so that he may be revealed in his own time.
53_2_7: For the mystery of lawlessness is already at work; only the One who now restrains will do so until He is taken out of the way.
53_2_8: And then the lawless one will be revealed — whom the Lord Jesus will slay with the breath of His mouth, and bring to nothing by the appearance of His coming.
53_2_9: The coming of the lawless one will be in accord with the working of Satan — with all power, and with signs and lying wonders,
53_2_10: and with all unrighteous deception for those who are perishing — because they refused to love the truth and so be saved.
53_2_11: For this reason, God sends them a working of error — so that they will believe the lie,
53_2_12: in order that all may be condemned who have not believed the truth, but have taken pleasure in unrighteousness.
53_2_13: But we are bound always to thank God for you, brothers beloved by the Lord — because God chose you from the beginning for salvation, through sanctification by the Spirit and faith in the truth,
53_2_14: to which He called you by our gospel — for the obtaining of the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ.
53_2_15: So then, brothers, stand firm — and hold to the traditions you were taught, whether by spoken word or by letter from us.
53_2_16: Now may our Lord Jesus Christ Himself, and God our Father — who has loved us and given us eternal comfort and good hope through grace —
53_2_17: comfort your hearts and establish you in every good word and work.
53_3_1: Finally, brothers, pray for us — that the word of the Lord may run swiftly and be glorified, just as it is with you,
53_3_2: and that we may be delivered from unreasonable and wicked men — for not all have the faith.
53_3_3: But the Lord is faithful. He will establish you and guard you from the evil one.
53_3_4: And we have confidence in the Lord concerning you — that you are doing, and will do, the things we command.
53_3_5: May the Lord direct your hearts into the love of God, and into the steadfastness of Christ.
53_3_6: Now we command you, brothers — in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ — that you withdraw from every brother who walks in disorder, and not according to the tradition that you received from us.
53_3_7: For you yourselves know how you ought to imitate us — because we did not behave disorderly among you,
53_3_8: nor did we eat anyone's bread without paying for it. Rather, with toil and labor we worked night and day, so as not to be a burden to any of you —
53_3_9: not because we have no right, but in order to give ourselves to you as a model to imitate.
53_3_10: For even when we were with you, we used to give you this command: "If anyone is not willing to work, neither shall he eat."
53_3_11: For we hear that some among you are walking in disorder — not working at all, but being busybodies.
53_3_12: Now such persons we command and exhort, in the Lord Jesus Christ, to work quietly and to eat their own bread.
53_3_13: But as for you, brothers — do not grow weary in doing what is right.
53_3_14: If anyone does not obey our word in this letter, take note of him and have nothing to do with him — so that he may be ashamed.
53_3_15: Yet do not regard him as an enemy, but admonish him as a brother.
53_3_16: Now may the Lord of peace Himself give you peace at all times, in every way. The Lord be with you all.
53_3_17: I, Paul, write this greeting with my own hand. This is the sign in every letter — this is how I write.
53_3_18: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
61_1_1: Simon Peter, a bondservant and apostle of Jesus Christ — to those who have obtained a faith of equal standing with ours, by the righteousness of our God and Savior Jesus Christ:
61_1_2: Grace and peace be multiplied to you in the knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord.
61_1_3: His divine power has granted to us all things pertaining to life and godliness, through the full knowledge of Him who called us by His own glory and excellence —
61_1_4: by which He has granted to us His precious and very great promises, so that through them you may become partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through evil desire.
61_1_5: For this very reason, make every effort to add to your faith virtue; and to virtue, knowledge;
61_1_6: and to knowledge, self-control; and to self-control, perseverance; and to perseverance, godliness;
61_1_7: and to godliness, brotherly affection; and to brotherly affection, love.
61_1_8: For if these qualities are yours and are increasing, they keep you from being ineffective or unfruitful in the full knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.
61_1_9: For the one who lacks these things is so nearsighted that he is blind — having forgotten the cleansing from his former sins.
61_1_10: Therefore, brothers, be all the more diligent to make your calling and election sure. For if you do these things, you will never stumble —
61_1_11: for in this way, the entrance into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ will be richly supplied to you.
61_1_12: For this reason I will always be ready to remind you of these things — though you know them, and are established in the truth that is with you.
61_1_13: I think it right, as long as I am in this body, to stir you up by way of reminder —
61_1_14: knowing that the laying aside of my body will be soon, just as our Lord Jesus Christ has made clear to me.
61_1_15: And I will make every effort, so that after my departure you will always be able to call these things to remembrance.
61_1_16: For we did not follow cleverly devised myths when we made known to you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ — but we were eyewitnesses of His majesty.
61_1_17: For when He received honor and glory from God the Father, when such a voice came to Him from the Majestic Glory: "This is My beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased" —
61_1_18: we ourselves heard this voice come from heaven when we were with Him on the holy mountain.
61_1_19: And we have the prophetic word made even more sure — to which you do well to pay attention, as to a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts.
61_1_20: Knowing this first: that no prophecy of Scripture comes from one's own interpretation.
61_1_21: For no prophecy was ever produced by the will of man — but men spoke from God as they were carried along by the Holy Spirit.
61_2_1: But there were also false prophets among the people, just as there will be false teachers among you — who will secretly bring in destructive heresies, even denying the Master who bought them — bringing on themselves swift destruction.
61_2_2: And many will follow their licentiousness, and because of them the way of truth will be blasphemed.
61_2_3: And in their greed they will exploit you with deceptive words. Their condemnation, from long ago, is not idle — and their destruction is not asleep.
61_2_4: For if God did not spare angels when they sinned, but cast them down to hell and committed them to chains of gloomy darkness, kept until the judgment;
61_2_5: and if He did not spare the ancient world, but preserved Noah, a herald of righteousness, with seven others, when He brought a flood upon the world of the ungodly;
61_2_6: and if He condemned the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah by reducing them to ashes, making them an example of what is going to happen to the ungodly;
61_2_7: and if He rescued righteous Lot, who was distressed by the licentious behavior of lawless men —
61_2_8: for as that righteous man lived among them day after day, his righteous soul was tormented by what he saw and heard of their lawless deeds —
61_2_9: then the Lord knows how to rescue the godly from trial, and how to keep the unrighteous under punishment for the day of judgment;
61_2_10: and especially those who walk according to the flesh in defiling lust, and who despise authority. Bold and arrogant, they are not afraid to revile glorious beings —
61_2_11: whereas angels, though greater in might and power, do not bring a reviling judgment against them before the Lord.
61_2_12: But these, like irrational animals, born of nature to be caught and destroyed — speaking abusively about things they do not understand — will also be destroyed in their corruption,
61_2_13: suffering wrong as the wages for doing wrong. They count it pleasure to revel in broad daylight. They are spots and blemishes, reveling in their own deceptions while they feast with you.
61_2_14: Their eyes are full of adultery and never cease from sin. They entice unsteady souls. They have hearts trained in greed — accursed children!
61_2_15: Forsaking the right way, they have gone astray. They have followed the way of Balaam, son of Beor, who loved the wages of unrighteousness —
61_2_16: but he was rebuked for his own transgression: a speechless donkey spoke with a man's voice and restrained the prophet's madness.
61_2_17: These are springs without water, and mists driven by a storm. The gloom of darkness has been reserved for them.
61_2_18: For when they speak arrogant, empty words, they entice — by lusts of the flesh, by sensuality — those who are barely escaping from the ones who live in error.
61_2_19: They promise them freedom, while they themselves are slaves of corruption — for whatever overcomes a man, by that he is enslaved.
61_2_20: For if, after escaping the defilements of the world through the full knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, they are again entangled in them and overcome — the last state has become worse for them than the first.
61_2_21: It would have been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness than, having known it, to turn back from the holy commandment delivered to them.
61_2_22: For them the true proverb has come true: "A dog returns to its own vomit," and, "A washed sow returns to wallowing in the mire."
61_3_1: This is now, beloved, the second letter I am writing to you — in both of which I am stirring up your sincere mind by way of reminder,
61_3_2: that you should remember the words spoken beforehand by the holy prophets, and the commandment of the Lord and Savior given through your apostles —
61_3_3: knowing this first: that scoffers will come in the last days, walking according to their own lusts,
61_3_4: and saying, "Where is the promise of His coming? For ever since the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of creation."
61_3_5: For they deliberately overlook this fact: that long ago by the word of God the heavens existed, and the earth was formed out of water and through water,
61_3_6: by which the world that then existed was destroyed by being flooded with water.
61_3_7: But by the same word, the present heavens and earth are stored up for fire — being kept until the day of judgment and the destruction of ungodly people.
61_3_8: But do not overlook this one fact, beloved: with the Lord, one day is as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.
61_3_9: The Lord is not slow concerning His promise, as some count slowness — but He is patient toward you, not wishing that any should perish, but that all should reach repentance.
61_3_10: But the day of the Lord will come like a thief — in which the heavens will pass away with a roar, and the elements will be dissolved with intense heat, and the earth and the works that are on it will be exposed.
61_3_11: Since all these things are to be dissolved in this way, what kind of people ought you to be — in holy conduct and godliness,
61_3_12: looking for and hastening the coming of the day of God, on account of which the heavens will be set on fire and dissolved, and the elements will melt with intense heat?
61_3_13: But according to His promise, we are looking for new heavens and a new earth — in which righteousness dwells.
61_3_14: Therefore, beloved — since you are looking for these things — be diligent to be found by Him in peace, spotless and blameless.
61_3_15: And consider the patience of our Lord as salvation — just as our beloved brother Paul also wrote to you, according to the wisdom given to him,
61_3_16: speaking of these things in all his letters — in which there are some things hard to understand, which the ignorant and unstable distort, as they do also the rest of the Scriptures, to their own destruction.
61_3_17: You therefore, beloved — knowing this beforehand — be on guard, so that you are not carried away by the error of the lawless and lose your own steadfastness.
61_3_18: But grow in the grace and full knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. To Him be the glory both now and to the day of eternity. Amen.
55_1_1: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, according to the promise of life that is in Christ Jesus —
55_1_2: to Timothy, my beloved son: Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
55_1_3: I thank God, whom I serve with a clear conscience as my forefathers did — as I constantly remember you in my prayers, night and day.
55_1_4: Recalling your tears, I long to see you, that I may be filled with joy.
55_1_5: I am reminded of the sincere faith within you — which first lived in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice, and now, I am persuaded, lives in you also.
55_1_6: For this reason I remind you to fan into flame the gift of God, which is in you through the laying on of my hands.
55_1_7: For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.
55_1_8: Therefore do not be ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me His prisoner — but share with me in suffering for the gospel, by the power of God,
55_1_9: who has saved us and called us with a holy calling — not according to our works, but according to His own purpose and the grace given to us in Christ Jesus before the ages of time began,
55_1_10: and now has been revealed through the appearing of our Savior Christ Jesus — who has abolished death and brought life and immortality to light through the gospel,
55_1_11: for which I was appointed a herald, an apostle, and a teacher.
55_1_12: For this reason I also suffer these things — but I am not ashamed, for I know whom I have believed, and I am persuaded that He is able to guard what I have entrusted to Him until that Day.
55_1_13: Hold fast the pattern of sound words that you have heard from me — in the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus.
55_1_14: Guard the good deposit entrusted to you, by the Holy Spirit who lives in us.
55_1_15: You know this: that all who are in Asia have turned away from me — among them Phygelus and Hermogenes.
55_1_16: May the Lord grant mercy to the household of Onesiphorus — for he often refreshed me, and was not ashamed of my chains.
55_1_17: But when he was in Rome, he sought me out diligently and found me.
55_1_18: May the Lord grant him to find mercy from the Lord on that Day. And you know very well how many ways he served at Ephesus.
55_2_1: You therefore, my son, be strong in the grace that is in Christ Jesus.
55_2_2: And the things you have heard from me through many witnesses — entrust these to faithful men, who will be able to teach others also.
55_2_3: Share in suffering, as a good soldier of Christ Jesus.
55_2_4: No one engaged in warfare entangles himself with the affairs of civilian life, so that he may please the one who enlisted him.
55_2_5: And if anyone competes in athletics, he is not crowned unless he competes according to the rules.
55_2_6: The hardworking farmer ought to be the first to share in the crops.
55_2_7: Consider what I say — for the Lord will give you understanding in everything.
55_2_8: Remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead, descended from David, according to my gospel —
55_2_9: for which I am suffering hardship to the point of being chained as a criminal. But the word of God is not chained.
55_2_10: Therefore I endure all things for the sake of the chosen ones — so that they too may obtain the salvation that is in Christ Jesus, with eternal glory.
55_2_11: This saying is faithful: For if we have died with Him, we shall also live with Him.
55_2_12: If we endure, we shall also reign with Him. If we deny Him, He also will deny us.
55_2_13: If we are faithless, He remains faithful — for He cannot deny Himself.
55_2_14: Remind them of these things — charging them in the presence of God not to wrangle about words. It is to no profit, only the ruin of those who hear.
55_2_15: Be diligent to present yourself approved to God — a worker who has no need to be ashamed, rightly handling the word of truth.
55_2_16: But avoid worldly and empty chatter, for it will lead to more ungodliness,
55_2_17: and their word will spread like gangrene. Among them are Hymenaeus and Philetus,
55_2_18: who have strayed from the truth — saying that the resurrection has already taken place. They are upsetting the faith of some.
55_2_19: Nevertheless, the firm foundation of God stands — having this seal: "The Lord knows those who are His," and, "Let everyone who names the name of the Lord turn away from unrighteousness."
55_2_20: Now in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and silver, but also of wood and earthenware — some for honorable use, some for common.
55_2_21: Therefore, if anyone cleanses himself from these things, he will be a vessel for honor — sanctified, useful to the Master, prepared for every good work.
55_2_22: Flee youthful lusts. And pursue righteousness, faith, love, peace — with those who call on the Lord out of a pure heart.
55_2_23: But have nothing to do with foolish and ignorant disputes — knowing that they generate strife.
55_2_24: And the Lord's bondservant must not be quarrelsome — but kind to all, able to teach, patient when wronged,
55_2_25: in gentleness correcting those who are in opposition. Perhaps God will grant them repentance, leading to a full knowledge of the truth,
55_2_26: and they may come to their senses — escaping the snare of the devil, who has held them captive to do his will.
55_3_1: But know this: that in the last days perilous times will come.
55_3_2: For people will be lovers of self, lovers of money, boastful, arrogant, abusive, disobedient to parents, ungrateful, unholy,
55_3_3: without natural affection, unforgiving, slanderers, without self-control, brutal, despisers of good,
55_3_4: treacherous, reckless, conceited — lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of God,
55_3_5: having a form of godliness, but denying its power. Avoid such people.
55_3_6: For from these are those who creep into households and captivate weak women weighed down with sins, led away by various lusts —
55_3_7: always learning, and never able to come to the full knowledge of the truth.
55_3_8: Just as Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, so these also oppose the truth — men of corrupt mind, disqualified concerning the faith.
55_3_9: But they will not advance further. For their folly will be plain to all, just as also that of those men became.
55_3_10: But you have followed my teaching, my conduct, my purpose, my faith, my patience, my love, my steadfastness,
55_3_11: my persecutions, my sufferings — what happened to me at Antioch, at Iconium, at Lystra. What persecutions I endured! Yet out of them all the Lord rescued me.
55_3_12: Indeed, all who desire to live godly in Christ Jesus will be persecuted.
55_3_13: But evil men and impostors will go from bad to worse — deceiving and being deceived.
55_3_14: But as for you — continue in the things you have learned and have been assured of, knowing from whom you have learned them.
55_3_15: And how from infancy you have known the holy Scriptures, which are able to make you wise for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus.
55_3_16: All Scripture is breathed out by God, and is profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, for training in righteousness —
55_3_17: so that the man of God may be complete, equipped for every good work.
55_4_1: I solemnly charge you in the presence of God and of Christ Jesus — who will judge the living and the dead, and by His appearing and His kingdom:
55_4_2: Preach the word. Be ready in season and out of season. Reprove, rebuke, exhort — with all patience and instruction.
55_4_3: For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine — but according to their own desires they will accumulate for themselves teachers, having itching ears.
55_4_4: And they will turn their ears away from the truth, and turn aside to myths.
55_4_5: But you, be sober in all things. Endure suffering. Do the work of an evangelist. Fulfill your ministry.
55_4_6: For I am already being poured out as a drink offering, and the time of my departure has come.
55_4_7: I have fought the good fight. I have finished the race. I have kept the faith.
55_4_8: Henceforth there is laid up for me the crown of righteousness, which the Lord — the righteous Judge — will give to me on that Day. And not only to me, but also to all who have loved His appearing.
55_4_9: Be diligent to come to me quickly.
55_4_10: For Demas, having loved this present world, has forsaken me and gone to Thessalonica. Crescens has gone to Galatia, Titus to Dalmatia.
55_4_11: Only Luke is with me. Get Mark and bring him with you, for he is useful to me for ministry.
55_4_12: Tychicus I have sent to Ephesus.
55_4_13: When you come, bring the cloak that I left at Troas with Carpus — and the books, especially the parchments.
55_4_14: Alexander the coppersmith did me much harm. The Lord will repay him according to his deeds.
55_4_15: You also be on guard against him — for he greatly opposed our message.
55_4_16: At my first defense, no one stood with me — all forsook me. May it not be charged against them.
55_4_17: But the Lord stood by me and strengthened me — so that through me the proclamation might be fully accomplished, and that all the Gentiles might hear it. And I was rescued from the lion's mouth.
55_4_18: And the Lord will rescue me from every evil deed, and bring me safely into His heavenly kingdom. To Him be the glory forever and ever. Amen.
55_4_19: Greet Prisca and Aquila, and the household of Onesiphorus.
55_4_20: Erastus stayed in Corinth. Trophimus I left sick at Miletus.
55_4_21: Be diligent to come before winter. Eubulus greets you, as do Pudens and Linus and Claudia, and all the brothers.
55_4_22: The Lord be with your spirit. Grace be with you all. Amen.
